control: Password authentication is not exposed to untrusted networks
evidence: 344631 failed password attempts from 1008 distinct external IPs
recommendation: Disable password login (PasswordAuthentication no), require key-based auth or MFA, and restrict port 22 to a VPN or allow-list.

control: Account lockout / rate limiting stops guessing after about 5 attempts
evidence: 1221 of 1265 attack episodes exceeded 5 attempts; 157 exceeded 50; worst episode 86294 attempts
recommendation: Deploy fail2ban or equivalent (ban after 5 failures / 10 min), lower MaxAuthTries, add network-level rate limiting.

control: Direct privileged (root/admin) SSH login is disabled
evidence: 332784 attempts against privileged accounts; 0 successful root logins
recommendation: Set PermitRootLogin no; use named accounts with sudo and session logging.

control: No successful login follows a run of failures from the same source
evidence: 1 successful login(s) preceded by >= 3 failures within 60 min
recommendation: Reset credentials and review session activity for the affected account(s); force MFA.

control: Monitoring covers the bulk of malicious authentication activity
evidence: Detection rules cover 99.2% of failed attempts
recommendation: Tune thresholds in config.py and forward alerts to the SIEM / ticketing queue.
reference: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.15, A.8.16; NIST CSF 2.0 DE.CM

control: sshd MaxAuthTries is consistent with the PAM retry limit
evidence: 37963 log entries show PAM ignoring its max-retries limit (sessions reached 6 tries against a limit of 3)
recommendation: Align sshd MaxAuthTries with the PAM limit so that lockout policy is actually enforced.
